tasks.short: Prepare and implement remedial learning programmes

steps.what: Prepare remedial programs from observed difficulties and appropriate subject-learning strategies
Implement remedial programs and adjust extra help according to student progress

tasks.design: Keep remedial programme design and delivery with the teacher, using approved resources in {DOCS} and {LMS}. Selecting an intervention and responding to progress remain professional decisions; no model assigns pupils to support pathways.
tasks.previous_blocker: Learning difficulties have different causes that require careful investigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing resources support the teacher; a safe replacement for programme judgement is not established here.
tasks.still_hard: Determine why the learner is struggling and whether support is helping.
tasks.human_edge: Adapt help while preserving confidence and appropriate challenge.
tasks.altitude: The teacher retains remedial planning, delivery and escalation responsibility.

reach.learn: Use work examples and progress observations to frame questions

evidence.claim: Remedial support requires contextual assessment and observation of how students respond, beyond generating practice text.

assumptions: Teacher gathers work examples and student explanations in s1; their full capture and interpretation effort remains.
Rewriting individual materials belongs to the separate adaptation task; its potential saving is not counted again in this programme view.
No new application or process creates maintenance work; no automatic diagnosis or support eligibility decision is introduced.
unknowns: Which approved interventions and specialist support are available
research_questions: What evidence would show that the selected extra help is addressing the actual difficulty?

incremental.description: No new remedial allocation or monitoring application

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=35+65=100. Programme judgement, preparation and delivery retain effort. Separate material-rewriting savings are not repeated.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Discuss pupil needs and progress with professionals

steps.what: Review relevant student observations and prepare questions for other professionals
Meet with other professionals to discuss individual students’ needs, progress and next actions

tasks.design: Use existing authorised {OTHER} pupil records and factual work examples for preparation, then keep the professional discussion with the teacher. No generated transcript or automated recommendation is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: Professionals need to compare explanations and agree feasible support.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records can inform the conversation without replacing it.
tasks.still_hard: Resolve differing interpretations and responsibility for follow-up.
tasks.human_edge: Explain classroom context and listen to specialist perspectives.
tasks.altitude: The teacher retains professional collaboration and action commitments.

reach.learn: Distinguish evidence, uncertainty and requested help

evidence.claim: A collaborative discussion cannot be treated as removed merely because pupil records can be retrieved.

assumptions: Teacher selects and verifies the brief in s1 with full effort retained; no free clean case summary is assumed.
Other professionals contribute their own existing preparation and meeting time, unchanged and excluded from focal savings.
Meeting scheduling and formal report production are separate tasks. No new system adds upkeep.
unknowns: Which professionals should participate and which records they may access
research_questions: Do discussions end with clear owners for the next actions?

incremental.description: No new collaboration software or data flow

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=25+75=100. Preparation and discussion retain effort; no participant time or hypothetical meeting removal is counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Discuss progress and resource needs with parents

steps.what: Prepare factual examples of the child’s progress and current resource needs
Meet with parents and guardians to discuss progress and agree priorities and resource needs

tasks.design: Prepare from existing {OTHER} pupil records, then retain the teacher’s direct discussion with parents and guardians. No generated account substitutes for hearing family concerns or agreeing priorities.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful priorities depend on information from both school and family.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records support preparation, without establishing a new labour-saving mechanism for the meeting.
tasks.still_hard: Resolve disagreement and determine what help is both appropriate and available.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust and make room for information absent from school records.
tasks.altitude: Teacher responsibility for the conversation and commitments stays unchanged.

reach.task: Help resolve resource needs raised by families
reach.learn: Clarify requested help without promising unavailable support

evidence.claim: Discussing priorities with families is relationship-based work rather than a report-generation task.

assumptions: Teacher gathers and checks notes in s1; no structured parent-priority feed is assumed.
Parents supply their perspectives during s2 and their participation time stays unchanged outside focal teacher labour.
Current consent, interpretation and access arrangements remain in force. No new recording or messaging process creates upkeep.
unknowns: Which family access or interpretation arrangements are needed
research_questions: Do families leave with the same understanding of the priorities and next steps as the teacher?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=20+80=100. Preparation and family dialogue retain full effort; no report-drafting or scheduling benefit is imported.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare required student and activity reports

steps.what: Verify reporting scope and relevant student and activity records
Prepare factual report tables and record extracts in the required report format
Add necessary commentary, check report meaning and submit the approved report

tasks.design: Configure the native report query in {OTHER}, the pupil record system, to populate factual tables in the approved {DOCS} layout. The teacher verifies scope and facts, writes evaluative commentary and approves the exact final report before internal submission.
tasks.previous_blocker: Copying existing marks and activity fields into repeat layouts consumes report preparation time.
tasks.enabler_now: A query and template can assemble existing authorised records without a language model.
tasks.still_hard: Explain what the results mean and avoid unsupported statements about pupils.
tasks.human_edge: Choose relevant context and qualify conclusions appropriately.

ambition.what: Generate the same factual view between formal report dates for review.

tasks.altitude: The teacher can obtain factual drafts on demand while retaining commentary and submission responsibility.

reach.task: Review report completeness and source traceability
reach.learn: Trace each reported value to the correct pupil and period

evidence.claim: ParnasSys demonstrates pupil-record and learning-goal functionality; suitability of a secondary school’s native reporting query remains to be checked.
Template assembly of verified existing records is a proposed deterministic design, not a measured local saving.

assumptions: S1 produces exact pupil_ids, subject_ids, reporting_period, activity_selection and source_revision references, including manual resolution of incomplete records; its full 30% remains.

Teachers and authorised staff create original results and activity records during existing assessment and record-maintenance work. That capture time is unchanged outside this report boundary; no new clean feed is assumed.
Administration supplies required layout and field definitions. S2 consumes only supported native fields; unsupported or missing facts revert to manual compilation with no saving for that portion.
Test native report functions first. No generated pupil commentary or automatically published report is introduced.
unknowns: Which factual fields and source revisions native reporting exposes
How much current report compilation is already automated
research_questions: Can the generated draft be traced cell by cell to the correct authorised source and reporting period?

already_counted.description: Write commentary, inspect report facts and approve submission

incremental.description: Validate changed report layouts and field meanings
Maintain query mappings and access restrictions

approvals.approved_version: Teacher approves exact final report revision including commentary, selected source versions and recipient; any content, source or recipient change invalidates approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Provisional E1: B=100; R=30+0+35=65; gross=35%; minus 2 focal upkeep gives 33% net. Low: reports already populate natively or sources are incomplete. High: repeated factual copying and layout work vanish; scope verification, commentary and approval retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Factual report assembly can become lighter while remedial teaching and conversations about pupil needs remain direct professional work.
reach: Agree support actions with professionals and families
Review report requirements with school administrators
role.ambitious_version: Generate checked factual drafts more often and keep attention on helping pupils and agreeing practical support.

job.title: Secondary School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education
